routes.name: Read a Redis key
routes.auth: CMS admin JWT + webcms + admin OTP
summary: **Read one Redis string value.** Returns the value stored under the exact key, unchanged (also JSON strings and empty strings).
Personal data: none by itself — but it returns or removes whatever the key holds, e.g. a user's cached profile or first name.
Same endpoint on the vernacular backend (`testapp.koode.co`); each service uses its own Redis connection and admin token.
headers: Marks a CMS web request (admin token from an OTP-verified admin).

stores.what: No data store with personal data is involved.

notes.title: Source
notes.text: Redis key API quick reference (Aisle Engineering, 2026-11-09); code `app/controllers/admin/redis_keys_controller.rb` (develop_new @ bd85044).

notes.title: Status codes
notes.text: **200** `{status:true, key, value}`. · **404** `{status:false, message:"Redis key not found"}`. · **422** Key holds a non-string value. · **400** `{status:false, message:"A non-blank string key is required", details:[{field:"key", …}]}` for a missing or blank key. · **401** Empty body: admin token, permission, device or CMS OTP check failed. · **503** Redis operation unavailable.

notes.title: Seen on staging 2026-11-09
notes.text: testa2: an unknown key gives GET 404 "Redis key not found" and DELETE 200 deleted:false; a missing or blank key gives 400; an associate-level admin gets 401 (permission); an admin who has not passed the CMS OTP gets 401.

notes.title: Good to know
notes.text: Key in the query string, no body; headers Authorization (CMS admin token) + webcms: true. The CMS OTP is a Google Authenticator code (POST /admin/authenticate_rotp); once passed it stays valid for that admin until logout. Wildcards are literal (no pattern delete). The audit log keeps only the SHA-256 of the key.

notes.title: Security
notes.text: Any admin with the Redis permission can read any key (including cached names) and delete any key, e.g. caches or config.

routes.name: Delete a Redis key
routes.auth: CMS admin JWT + webcms + admin OTP
summary: **Delete one exact Redis key.** Works for any Redis data type; an absent key is not an error.
Personal data: none by itself — but it returns or removes whatever the key holds, e.g. a user's cached profile or first name.
Same endpoint on the vernacular backend (`testapp.koode.co`); each service uses its own Redis connection and admin token.
